title: Levy of GST
keywords: levy tax charge rate supplier liable
text: GST is levied on intra-state supplies of goods or services at notified rates on the transaction value (Sec 15). The supplier is liable to pay it, except where the law shifts liability to the recipient under reverse charge.

title: Reverse charge (RCM)
citation: Sec 9(3) and 9(4) CGST Act; Sec 5(3) and 5(4) IGST Act
keywords: reverse charge rcm recipient liable pay notified
text: For categories of supplies notified by the Government, the recipient (not the supplier) pays the GST. RCM tax has to be paid in cash through the electronic cash ledger; it cannot be paid by using input tax credit (Sec 49(4)). The recipient can claim the same amount as ITC once paid, if the purchase is for business and ITC is otherwise allowed.

title: Import of services is under reverse charge
keywords: import services foreign vendor overseas non-resident rcm igst software saas subscription
text: Services supplied by a person located outside India to a recipient in India (other than a non-taxable online recipient) are notified for reverse charge: the Indian recipient pays IGST. It is reported in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d), paid in cash, and then claimed as ITC in Table 4(A)(2) 'import of services'.

title: Import of services - definition
keywords: import of services definition supplier outside india recipient place of supply
text: 'Import of services' means a supply where the supplier is located outside India, the recipient is located in India, and the place of supply is in India. All three conditions must hold.

title: Export of services - five conditions
keywords: export services conditions foreign exchange convertible recipient outside india zero rated lut
text: A supply of services is an 'export' only if: (i) the supplier is in India, (ii) the recipient is outside India, (iii) the place of supply is outside India, (iv) payment is received in convertible foreign exchange (or in INR where RBI permits), and (v) the supplier and recipient are not merely establishments of the same person. Miss any one and it is an ordinary taxable supply.

title: Zero-rated supplies
keywords: zero rated export sez refund lut bond igst without payment
text: Exports of goods or services and supplies to SEZs are zero-rated. You may export without paying IGST under a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) and claim a refund of unutilised ITC, or pay IGST and claim a refund of that tax. In GSTR-3B they appear in Table 3.1(b).

title: Letter of Undertaking (LUT)
keywords: lut letter of undertaking export bond rfd-11 validity
text: To export without paying IGST you furnish a LUT in Form GST RFD-11 before the export. It is valid for the financial year for which it is given, so renew it each year, and exports made without a valid LUT must be taxed.

title: Place of supply of services (cross-border)
keywords: place of supply services location recipient outside india cross border
text: Where the supplier or the recipient is outside India, the place of supply of services is generally the location of the recipient (Sec 13(2)), subject to specific exceptions such as immovable property, events and performance-based services.

title: Eligibility for input tax credit
keywords: itc input tax credit eligible conditions invoice receipt paid supplier return 2b
text: ITC is allowed only if you hold a tax invoice or debit note, you have received the goods/services, the tax has actually been paid to the Government by the supplier, you have filed your return, and the invoice appears in your GSTR-2B (Sec 16(2)(aa)). If you do not pay the supplier within 180 days of the invoice date, the ITC must be reversed (2nd proviso to Sec 16(2)) and can be re-claimed after payment.

title: ITC only if the invoice is in GSTR-2B
keywords: 2b gstr-2b itc vendor not filed gstr-1 appear
text: Credit can be taken only for invoices whose details have been furnished by the supplier and communicated to you in GSTR-2B. If your vendor has not filed GSTR-1 for the month, their invoice will not be in your GSTR-2B and you cannot claim the credit that month. An older invoice that first appears in this month's 2B is claimable now; a line marked 'ITC not available' is not.

title: Time limit for claiming ITC
keywords: itc time limit november deadline annual return late
text: ITC for an invoice must be claimed by 30 November following the end of the financial year to which the invoice relates, or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier. After that the credit is lost.

title: Blocked credits
keywords: blocked ineligible itc food beverages motor vehicle club membership health insurance works contract gifts personal
text: ITC is not available on, among others: motor vehicles for carrying up to 13 persons (with exceptions), food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, club memberships, rent-a-cab and life/health insurance (with exceptions), works-contract services for immovable property (other than plant and machinery), goods lost, stolen or given as gifts, and personal consumption.

title: Time to issue a tax invoice
keywords: invoice timing 30 days services issue tax invoice
text: For services, the tax invoice must be issued within 30 days of supply (45 days for banks and financial institutions). A registered person must issue invoices in the prescribed format with a serial number unique for the financial year.

title: GSTR-1 - outward supplies statement
keywords: gstr-1 gstr1 outward supplies 11th due b2b b2c exports hsn
text: A monthly filer reports all outward supplies in GSTR-1 by the 11th of the next month: B2B invoices by recipient GSTIN, large B2C invoices, exports, credit/debit notes, HSN summary and documents issued. Recipients' ITC depends on what you report here.

title: GSTR-3B - summary return and tax payment
keywords: gstr-3b gstr3b return pay tax 20th due summary 3.1 table
text: GSTR-3B is the monthly summary return, due by the 20th of the next month for most taxpayers. The tax payable is paid with the return: ITC is used first as the law permits, and the balance in cash. Table 3.1 reports outward supplies and reverse-charge inward supplies; Table 4 reports ITC; Table 6.1 shows payment.

title: Late fee
keywords: late fee penalty delay gstr-1 gstr-3b per day
text: Delay in filing GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B attracts a late fee of ₹50 per day (₹20 per day for nil returns), split equally between CGST and SGST, subject to caps notified by the Government according to turnover. The fee is payable in cash.

title: Payment of tax and use of ITC
keywords: set off utilisation itc cash ledger igst cgst sgst order payment
text: ITC of IGST is used first against IGST, then CGST, then SGST. CGST credit is used against CGST and then IGST; SGST credit against SGST and then IGST; CGST credit cannot pay SGST or vice versa. Tax payable under reverse charge cannot be paid from the credit ledger - it must be paid in cash (Sec 49(4)).

title: Order of utilisation of IGST credit
keywords: order igst credit first cgst sgst utilise
text: IGST credit has to be used up first: towards IGST liability, and the rest towards CGST and SGST in any order or proportion (CBIC Circular 98/17/2019-GST) - only after that can CGST or SGST credit be used. CGST credit then pays CGST, then IGST; SGST credit pays SGST, then IGST. Because the split of IGST credit between CGST and SGST is free, it should go where your own CGST/SGST credit falls short, so that no cash is paid while credit is left over.

title: Interest on late payment and wrong ITC
keywords: interest 18 percent 24 percent late payment wrong itc
text: Interest at 18% per annum is payable on tax paid late (on the net cash liability for the delay period). Interest at 24% per annum applies where ITC was wrongly availed and utilised or excess output tax was reduced.

title: GSTR-2B
keywords: gstr-2b 2b auto drafted statement 14th itc statement download json
text: GSTR-2B is an auto-generated, static statement of the ITC available to you for a month, based on your suppliers' GSTR-1/5/6 and ISD filings. It is generated around the 14th of the following month and is the basis for claiming ITC in GSTR-3B Table 4. The portal lets you download it as JSON or Excel.

title: HSN/SAC codes in GSTR-1
keywords: hsn sac code digits summary table 12
text: Taxpayers must report HSN/SAC codes in the GSTR-1 HSN summary (Table 12): 4 digits up to ₹5 crore turnover, 6 digits above. From the May 2025 period the portal only accepts codes picked from its HSN list (no free text), and nil-rated/exempt supplies are part of the summary. Software and IT services are generally under SAC 9983 (e.g. 998314 IT design and development, 998315 hosting).

title: B2CL threshold
keywords: b2cl b2c large inter-state unregistered threshold
text: Inter-state supplies to unregistered persons are reported invoice-wise (B2CL) when the invoice value exceeds the notified threshold (₹1,00,000 from 1 Aug 2024); smaller ones are reported as state-wise B2CS totals. Account0 assumes this threshold - confirm it with your CA.

title: TDS on salary
keywords: salary tds employer deduct estimate average rate monthly
text: An employer deducts tax from salary every month based on the employee's estimated total income for the year, at average rates. The tax for the year is estimated, TDS deducted so far is subtracted, and the balance is spread over the remaining months. Form 16 is issued by 15 June after year end.

title: New tax regime slabs (FY 2025-26)
keywords: new regime slabs standard deduction 75000 cess rates
text: Under the default new regime for FY 2025-26: nil up to ₹4,00,000; 5% to ₹8,00,000; 10% to ₹12,00,000; 15% to ₹16,00,000; 20% to ₹20,00,000; 25% to ₹24,00,000; 30% above. Salaried employees get a standard deduction of ₹75,000. Health and education cess of 4% is added. Account0 assumes these slabs for later years - confirm after each Budget.

title: Rebate under Sec 87A (new regime)
keywords: rebate 87a 12 lakh zero tax marginal relief
text: For residents under the new regime, taxable income up to ₹12,00,000 (FY 2025-26) gets a rebate of up to ₹60,000 - so no tax is payable. Just above ₹12 lakh, marginal relief limits the tax to the amount by which income exceeds ₹12 lakh.

title: TDS on payments to contractors
keywords: 194c contractor works contract labour transport advertising 1 percent 2 percent
text: Payments to resident contractors/sub-contractors: TDS at 1% if the payee is an individual/HUF, 2% otherwise. Deduction applies if a single payment exceeds ₹30,000 or total payments in the year exceed ₹1,00,000.

title: TDS on professional and technical fees
keywords: 194j professional technical fees director consultant 10 percent 2 percent
text: Fees for professional services and royalty: 10%, threshold ₹50,000 per payee in a year (from 1 Apr 2025). Fees for technical services and call-centre: 2%, same threshold. Remuneration, fees or commission to a DIRECTOR (other than salary, 194J(1)(ba)): 10% with NO threshold. A professional is, for example, a lawyer, CA, architect or consultant; whether your vendor is 'technical' or 'professional' is a judgement you confirm.

title: TDS on rent
keywords: 194i rent land building machinery 10 percent 2 percent office monthly 50000 per month 393 1008 1009
text: Rent: 2% for plant, machinery and equipment; 10% for land, building and furniture. From 1 Apr 2025 TDS applies when the rent exceeds ₹50,000 for a month or part of a month (earlier ₹2,40,000 a year). Under the Income-tax Act 2025 (from 1 Apr 2026) rent is in the s.393(1) table, payment codes 1008 (plant & machinery) and 1009 (land/building) - verify codes with your CA.

title: TDS on commission or brokerage
keywords: 194h commission brokerage 2 percent
text: Commission or brokerage (not for securities): 2% (reduced from 5% from 1 Oct 2024). Threshold ₹20,000 per year (from 1 Apr 2025).

title: TDS on purchase of goods
keywords: 194q purchase goods 50 lakh 0.1 percent turnover 10 crore
text: A buyer whose turnover in the preceding year exceeded ₹10 crore deducts 0.1% on purchases from a resident seller above ₹50 lakh in the year (on the excess only).

title: TDS on payments to non-residents
keywords: 195 non resident foreign payment remittance 15ca 15cb dtaa treaty equalisation levy google ads saas
text: Payments to non-residents that are chargeable to tax in India require TDS at the rate in force or the treaty rate, supported by Forms 15CA/15CB. Whether a foreign SaaS or services payment is taxable in India depends on the nature of the payment and the treaty, so Account0 does not compute it - take your CA's advice before remitting. There is no equalisation levy on foreign SaaS or online vendors any more: the 2% levy on e-commerce supplies was abolished from 1 Aug 2024 and the 6% levy on online advertising from 1 Apr 2025.

title: Higher TDS rate without PAN
keywords: pan not available 20 percent higher rate 397 5 percent 194q salary average rate
text: If the payee does not furnish a PAN, TDS is deducted at the higher of the normal rate, the rate in force, or 20% - but 5% for purchase of goods (194Q). For salary, the higher of 20% and the average rate, and nil if no tax is payable. From 1 Apr 2026 the same rule is s.397(2) Income-tax Act 2025 (verify exact rates with your CA).

title: Disallowance for non-deduction of TDS
keywords: disallowance 30 percent expense tds not deducted
text: If TDS was required but not deducted (or not deposited by the due date for filing the return), 30% of the expense is disallowed as a deduction in computing the company's profit.

title: Interest on late TDS
keywords: interest tds late deduction deposit 1 percent 1.5 percent per month
text: Interest is 1% per month from the date TDS was deductible to the date it is deducted, and 1.5% per month from deduction to deposit; each part-month counts as a full month.

title: TDS deposit due dates
keywords: tds deposit 7th challan 281 due date march 30 april
text: TDS deducted in a month is deposited by the 7th of the following month (30 April for March) using Challan 281.

title: Quarterly TDS statements
keywords: 24q 26q quarterly tds return statement due dates 31 july october january may
text: TDS statements are filed quarterly: Form 24Q for salaries and 26Q for other resident payments, due 31 Jul, 31 Oct, 31 Jan and 31 May. Certificates (Form 16A) follow 15 days after the due date; Form 16 by 15 June.

title: Fee for late TDS statements
keywords: 234e late fee tds statement 200 per day
text: A late TDS statement attracts a fee of ₹200 per day until filed, capped at the TDS amount of the statement.

title: Rounding of tax amounts
keywords: rounding rupee nearest
text: Sec 288B rounds the tax payable or refundable by a taxpayer to the nearest ₹10. It is not the rule for TDS: TDS is in practice rounded to the nearest rupee (as the TDS returns and challans require whole rupees).

title: TDS on invoices with GST shown separately
keywords: tds gst component excluded invoice shown separately base
text: If GST is shown separately in the invoice, TDS under Chapter XVII-B is deducted on the amount excluding GST. If GST is not separately indicated, TDS applies to the whole amount.

title: MSME payments - deduction only on payment
keywords: msme 45 days payment micro small enterprises deduction
text: An expense owed to a micro or small enterprise is deductible only in the year it is actually paid if the payment is made after the agreed time (maximum 45 days; 15 days if there is no written agreement). Check whether your vendors are registered MSMEs.

title: Advance tax
keywords: advance tax installments 15 june september december march 10000 interest
text: Where the year's tax liability is ₹10,000 or more, advance tax is paid by 15 June (15%), 15 Sep (45%), 15 Dec (75%) and 15 Mar (100%). Shortfalls attract interest under Sec 234B and 234C.

title: Income-tax return of a company
keywords: itr-6 income tax return company due date 31 october audit
text: A company files ITR-6 electronically, due 31 October after the year end (30 November if transfer pricing reports are required). Where a tax audit applies (Sec 44AB), the audit report is due one month earlier, 30 September.

title: Annual General Meeting
keywords: agm annual general meeting six months 30 september
text: A company must hold its AGM within six months of the financial year end (by 30 September for a 31 March year end). Other ROC filing dates are counted from the AGM date.

title: Filing financial statements (AOC-4)
keywords: aoc-4 financial statements roc 30 days agm late fee
text: Within 30 days of the AGM the company files its adopted financial statements in Form AOC-4. Delay attracts additional fees of ₹100 per day with no cap.

title: Annual return (MGT-7 / MGT-7A)
keywords: mgt-7 mgt-7a annual return 60 days small company
text: The annual return is filed within 60 days of the AGM - Form MGT-7A for small companies and one-person companies, Form MGT-7 for others.

title: Auditor appointment (ADT-1)
keywords: adt-1 auditor appointment 15 days
text: A company files Form ADT-1 within 15 days of the AGM at which an auditor is appointed or re-appointed.

title: DIR-3 KYC for directors
citation: Rule 12A, Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014, as amended by G.S.R. 943(E)
keywords: dir-3 kyc director din deactivated 30 june three years 3 year cycle
text: Under the amended Rule 12A (G.S.R. 943(E), 31 Dec 2025, effective 31 Mar 2026) every person holding a DIN files DIR-3 KYC once every three financial years, by 30 June, instead of every year by 30 September. A KYC is also needed within 30 days whenever the director's mobile number, e-mail or residential address changes. A missed filing deactivates the DIN until a fee of ₹5,000 is paid.

title: RCM (reverse charge) - in plain words
keywords: rcm reverse charge meaning plain simple
text: Normally the seller charges GST and pays it to the Government. Under reverse charge you, the buyer, work out and pay the GST yourself and then claim it back as input credit. For a foreign SaaS or consulting vendor this happens every month.

title: LUT - in plain words
keywords: lut letter undertaking meaning plain simple export
text: A yearly declaration on the GST portal that lets you invoice exports without charging IGST. Without a valid LUT you must charge 18% IGST on the export and claim a refund later.

title: Input tax credit - in plain words
keywords: itc input credit meaning plain simple set off
text: The GST you paid on business purchases that you may subtract from the GST you collect on sales. Only valid if the invoice is genuine, the vendor has filed, and the credit is not blocked.

title: Set-off in GSTR-3B - in plain words
keywords: set off offset liability credit ledger cash ledger plain simple
text: Your GST liability is first reduced by available input credit following set rules (IGST credit must be used up first, and can be split between CGST and SGST as needed); what is left is paid in cash. RCM tax is always paid in cash.

title: TAN
keywords: tan tax deduction account number
text: Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number - a 10-character number every deductor needs to quote in TDS challans and returns.

title: DSC and EVC
keywords: dsc evc digital signature electronic verification code filing authentication portal
text: Returns on the GST/income-tax portals are authenticated with a Digital Signature Certificate (mandatory for companies on GST) or an Electronic Verification Code sent to the registered mobile/email (where permitted).

title: Place of supply
keywords: place of supply pos state intra inter igst cgst sgst
text: The state or territory where a supply is taxed. If the supplier's state and the place of supply are the same, CGST+SGST apply; if different, IGST applies.

title: B2B, B2CL, B2CS
keywords: b2b b2c b2cl b2cs unregistered registered customers
text: B2B means sales to GST-registered businesses (invoice-wise reporting). B2C means sales to unregistered customers: large inter-state invoices are reported individually (B2CL); everything else is summarised by state and rate (B2CS).

title: Why Account0 asks you to confirm tax treatment
keywords: confirm tax treatment never guess llm extraction why
text: Account0 reads documents with AI but never decides tax treatment. Supply type, reverse charge, GST rate and ITC eligibility are always confirmed by you (or by a rule you created from an earlier confirmation) because they determine tax and penalties. All tax figures are then computed by plain deterministic code.

title: Why filed months are locked
keywords: lock period filed edit unlock audit
text: Once a return is filed, the figures have been reported to the Government. Locking the month stops silent edits that would make your books disagree with the filed return; unlocking requires a reason that is kept in the audit trail.

title: Time of supply under reverse charge
keywords: time of supply reverse charge rcm 60 days payment date import of services when liable
text: For services under reverse charge (including import of services) the time of supply is the earlier of the date of payment and the date immediately after sixty days from the supplier's invoice. If the supplier is an associated enterprise abroad, it is the earlier of the entry in your books and the payment. The RCM tax goes into the GSTR-3B of that month, and its ITC follows the payment of that tax.

title: Reversal of ITC when the supplier is not paid in 180 days
citation: Rule 37 CGST Rules; Sec 16(2) second proviso
keywords: 180 days unpaid supplier reverse itc 4b2 reclaim 4d1 interest
text: If you do not pay a supplier (value plus tax) within 180 days of the invoice date, the ITC taken on it must be reversed in GSTR-3B Table 4B(2) with interest. Once you pay, the credit can be re-claimed (shown in 4D(1)).

title: Renewing the LUT for exports
citation: Rule 96A CGST Rules; Form GST RFD-11
keywords: lut renewal rfd-11 export without payment every year 1 april
text: A Letter of Undertaking (Form GST RFD-11) lets you export without paying IGST. It is valid for one financial year, so file a new one before 1 April each year; otherwise exports must be made with payment of IGST and the tax claimed back as a refund.
